For example, if the Rams face the Bengals, and oddsmakers set the spread at Rams -3.5, you would need Los Angeles to win by 4 or more points in order to cash your Rams bet. What is an Over/Under Bet? Over/Under is a wager based on how many points you think will be scored in a specific game. Oddsmakers set the total, and bettors decide whether the final score will be higher or lower than that number. If an Over/Under is set at 44.5 points and you bet Over, you will need the combined score of both teams to be 45 points or higher to win your bet. What is a Moneyline Bet? A moneyline bet involves choosing which team you believe will win a specific matchup. The moneyline favorite carries a minus designation, like -130. This means that you need to wager $130 to earn a $100 profit. Conversely, the underdog carries a plus designation, like +110. This means that you win $110 in profit on a $100 bet. highlights: Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: finding betting value. Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game-winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, favorite defensive props and the top game to bet in Week 3. I tend to stay away from double-digit spreads in this league (especially for road favorites).

The Bucs have had Robinson on the field on just 23% of clear pass rushing situations this season, down from 52% last year in Carolina. Other sack bets I recommend: Jaelan Phillips UNDER 0.75 sacks (+125) Leonard Williams UNDER 0.25 sacks (-109) Chris Jones UNDER 0.25 sacks (-138) Andrew Van Ginkel UNDER 0.25 sacks (-128) Donovan Ezeiruaku UNDER 4.5 tackles + assists (-107) Ezeiruaku has been playing a little more this season -- 65% of snaps this year vs. 55% last year -- but that's not nearly enough to overcome this high line for an edge rusher. I think what's happening here is this line is being inflated by an outlandish 10-tackle game in Week 1. But it was only the third time Ezeiruaku had ever gone over 4.5 combined tackles in his career.

If Ezeiruaku's role had changed substantially in addition to the slight uptick in playing time this would be a different story, but he's still playing as a 7 or 9 technique 93% of the time (was 89% last year). And Ezeiruaku's tackle rate was almost exactly average for an edge rusher last year. I think the under here is an excellent value. Jordyn Brooks UNDER 9.5 tackles + assists (-116) It's pretty easy to imagine how Brooks could accrue a gaudy tackle number in this game. The Chiefs are double-digit favorites, have been having success with the ground game and if they get out to a big lead they'll simply run the ball to run out the clock. The result? Plenty of tackle opportunities for Miami's defense, and in particular a linebacker like Brooks. But the model knows all that and says this line is just far too high. Just last week Miami was massive underdogs to the 49ers and Brooks recorded just three combined tackles. I would bet this down to -150.

You can also consider Love to pass for 100+ yards (-125) in each half if the juice on the touchdowns isn't your speed. Given the high tax on the success rate, oddsmakers are clearly expecting the young quarterback to sling two touchdowns against Carolina. Love has thrown at least two touchdowns in three out of four home games dating back to last season. Chuba Hubbard Anytime Touchdown Scorer (-115) You can throw away Chuba Hubbard’s performance last week in what was a complete nightmare for the Carolina Panthers. Hubbard rushed for a season-low seven attempts. Before Sunday, Hubbard scored three touchdowns in two games. The Panthers running back has scored in four out of six games. Carolina had made a strong effort to get the running game going over the last three weeks - before playing Tampa on Sunday. Hubbard rushed for 67 carries over three contests, with at least 19 attempts per contest. Jalen Coker and Tetairoa McMillan have combined for four touchdowns this season and haven’t crossed the goal line since Week 4. If Carolina wants to meet its expectation of 22+ points, we expect Hubbard to account for at least one touchdown. Josh Jacobs 3+ Receptions (-135)

Our next selection is somewhat surprising given the immediate role Josh Jacobs played in the passing game on Sunday. In his first game back, Jacobs was targeted on seven passes and caught five. His receiving yardage prop is highly tempting at 20+ for a +105 return. Ultimately, we are going to play it safe and back Jacobs’ receptions. Since last season, Jacobs has finished with three or more receptions in six out of the last 10 games. The Green Bay running back caught four passes in the Packers’ loss to the Panthers last season. Jordan Love has attempted 86 passes over the previous two contests. With that volume, Jacobs is a strong candidate to reach the three-reception threshold. Savion Williams 25+ Receiving Yards (-114) We close out the night with our sweatiest selection of all. Savion Williams has cleared 25 yards in two consecutive games. With limited options at wide receiver for Green Bay, Williams is being asked to take on a bigger role. He has responded with 69 yards in the last two games.

results.description: Geoff Schwartz’s best Week 10 bets include the Vikings covering in Kirk Cousins’ return and a player prop he loves in 49ers-Cowboys.
highlights: 2026 NFL Week 10 Best Bets, Expert Picks: Back Vikings in Kirk Cousins’ Return Who knew that Kirk Cousins would be all the rage in NFL Week 10? Here is how I'm wagering the weekend in the professional football ranks. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports. I think wagering on a side or total for a Cowboys game is a foolish decision. You never know what you’re getting from this team. What I do know about this game is that the 49ers will use Christian McCaffrey as they normally do. CMC had 18 carries last week and an additional three targets through the air. That’s 21 attempts to gain yards in a game the Niners won by multiple touchdowns. In the last two close games the 49ers have played, CMC got 16 carries and 10 targets.

The Packers have been outstanding at throwing down the field. Jordan Love has been bombing the ball to his receivers, and although the rushing game isn’t great, Green Bay is scoring enough points. The defense has also played better than expected, shutting down nearly every offense it has faced this season. I like the Vikings to cover this game for a few reasons. For starters, just having Cousins in the lineup will reinvigorate the Vikings, and it wouldn’t surprise me to see Justin Jefferson have his best game of the season. I also like the matchup of the Vikings’ defense against the Packers’ offensive line, which is mediocre. Minnesota's pressure packages will be difficult to handle. Geoff Schwartz Schwartz's Pick: Vikings +3

I’d imagine this game will see the 49ers looking to put up some numbers, as the Cowboys' offense will probably look to do the same, since the defense can't ... defend. The Dallas defense ranks 31st against the rush, and it is middle-of-the-pack in receiving yards allowed to running backs. However, Dallas doesn’t face many teams that want to pass to the running back as much as the 49ers do. Geoff Schwartz Schwartz's Pick: Christian McCaffrey Over 99.5 rushing and receiving yards The Vikings traded for quarterback Kirk Cousins on Tuesday to help fix their offensive woes. He’s an immediate upgrade over what the Vikings had at QB with Carson Wentz and Kyler Murray. And while Cousins is probably average at best right now, that’s all the Vikings need at that position. The Vikings’ defense and special teams are elite. Minnesota just needs an offense that can move the ball enough to score points, so the defense doesn’t have to be perfect to win games. This move might actually allow the Vikings’ defense to play even better.
